Mortgages A VA loan could save veterans over $2,000 on mortgage payments annually — here are our favorite lenders
 See how VA loan payments compare with conventional mortgages and our top lender picks.
 Published Tue, Nov 10 2026 Kelsey Neubauer Reporter, CNBC Select Share Share Article via Facebook Share Article via Twitter Share Article via LinkedIn Share Article via Email Homebuyers who have served or are currently serving in the military can save thousands in housing payments annually by using a VA loan benefit , which offers rates lower than conventional mortgages and doesn't require private mortgage insurance.
 Despite that, not all eligible military members use the benefit. Fifty-five percent of veteran homebuyers used a VA loan to fund their purchase in 2025, while one-third used a conventional mortgage instead, according to the National Association of Realtors .
 This could be a missed opportunity. A CNBC Select analysis found that a borrower taking out the average VA loan amount in 2025, which was $390,101 — according to an analysis of VA data by Rocket Mortgage and Redfin — could have saved $2,601.84 annually in housing payments with a VA loan compared to a conventional mortgage.
 To reach that conclusion, we compared monthly principal and interest payments on a 30-year fixed-rate VA loan and a conventional mortgage using the $390,101 loan amount. We used the average VA and conventional mortgage rates as of Nov. 4, per Optimal Blue. 
 In both scenarios, we determined the buyer had enough cash for a 10% down payment. For the conventional mortgage, we added annual private mortgage insurance equal to 0.5% of the loan balance, divided into monthly payments — because a conventional loan borrower who puts down less than 20% must purchase PMI. 
 In the VA loan equation, we did not include the VA funding fee in the comparison because it is typically a one-time fee. We then multiplied the monthly payment difference by 12 to estimate the annual savings.
 Savings will vary based on loan size, interest rate and other factors. To get the lowest rate possible, strengthen your credit and save up for a large down payment .

 Best VA lenders
 If you're interested in a VA loan, CNBC Select has reviewed dozens of lenders who offer the product, including companies that dedicate their entire business to loans for veterans. Veterans United and Navy Federal Credit Union are two of our favorites. 
 In addition to its full suite of VA loans, Veterans United has a foundation that partners with local and national charities like Avalon Action Alliance, an organization dedicated to supporting veterans' mental and physical health, and Blue Star Families, which connects military families with resources and community support. 
 Additionally, Veterans United has excellent customer service. It earns high ratings in J.D. Power surveys and from the Better Business Bureau.
